master.tagline: The world runs. Farmers feed. Deere equips.

investment_thesis.summary: Deere is a dominant agricultural and construction equipment franchise with industry-leading distribution, brand power, and a growing technology ecosystem. The investment debate is whether precision agriculture, autonomy, lifecycle solutions and proprietary data can materially improve through-cycle earnings quality beyond what a normal agricultural recovery would deliver. Management's long-term framework points toward stronger margins, higher operating returns and mid-cycle EPS of roughly $40-45 by 2030. The complication is valuation: with the stock around the low-$600s and trading far above Deere's historical mid-cycle multiple, investors are already paying for both a cyclical recovery and some structural re-rating. The thesis therefore requires technology attach, C&F execution and farmer economics to translate into measurable P&L improvement rather than remaining a strategic narrative.
investment_thesis.core_question: Can technology-enabled solutions lift mid-cycle EPS to $40-45 by 2030 and justify a structurally higher multiple?
what_market_prices_in: A full agricultural recovery from the 2026 trough
Higher through-cycle equipment margins and returns
A sustained premium valuation for technology and recurring economics
what_must_be_true: Precision-ag attach and engagement must rise materially
Farmer income and replacement demand must stabilize
C&F excavator launch and supply tightening must lift profitability
falsification: Software/lifecycle monetization stays immaterial despite engagement
Mid-cycle valuation reverts toward historical norms before earnings catch up
investment_thesis.variant_view: Technology can improve Deere's earnings quality, but the stock may be discounting that outcome earlier than the P&L proves it.

company_overview.summary: Deere designs, manufactures and distributes equipment and technology across agriculture, construction, forestry and turf. Agriculture remains the economic core, while Construction & Forestry provides diversification and Financial Services supports customer purchases. Deere's dealer network, installed base, precision-ag hardware/software and proprietary farm data create a lifecycle ecosystem that can monetize customers beyond the original equipment sale.

financial_snapshot.valuation_comment: The market appears to price in a full earnings recovery plus meaningful structural re-rating.
financial_bullets: Operating ROA: ~30%+ with a 45% long-term target.
EPS: ~$18-20 at 2026 trough; $40-45 mid-cycle target by 2030.
Free Cash Flow: ~$5B+ in a normal-cycle framework.
Net Debt / EBITDA: ~1.0x, supporting a conservative balance sheet.

earnings_history.cycle_note: Last four cycles: trough-to-peak revenue growth ~65% average; management targets ~75% next cycle.

valuation_scenarios.logic: Technology lifts margins and earnings resilience.

signposts.why_it_matters: Adoption scale drives recurring revenue and stickiness.
Tests C&F share gains and profitability.

catalysts.why_it_matters: Tests C&F share gains and integrated precision technology.
Determines timing of the earnings inflection.

thesis_threats.watch_for: Commodity prices stay low through '27; farmer balance sheets weaken; retail sales keep falling; trough >36 mos.
SaaS <5% of sales by '28; engaged acres <40% highly engaged; farmers resist subscriptions.
Peak EPS < $40; recovery delayed 12–24 mos.; multiple re-rates to 15–20x mid-cycle.
Tariffs >80% of historical burden; cost inflation outpaces pricing; tech attach drops; C&F margins miss.

master.final_takeaway: Deere combines a best-in-class franchise with a credible technology roadmap. The stock already discounts a lot. The investment hinges on execution: turning early technology leadership and a C&F inflection into structurally higher margins and $40-45 mid-cycle EPS by 2030.
master.bottom_line: Great company, cyclical timing, execution risk.
